problemSummary: Analysts and mandate leads at boutique advisory firms struggle to turn CIMs, filings, notes, and data-room files into a briefing a partner can defend, because search is fragmented across drives, PDFs, and generic chat tools that lack citations and client isolation. That results in slow time-to-insight, uncited claims, and leakage risk. Today they Ctrl-F documents and rebuild memos by hand at a cost of many hours per mandate plus reputational risk.

personas.name: Managing Partner
personas.primaryJob: Ship client-ready advice without leaking other clients' materials
personas.successMetric: Time-to-cited-briefing down; zero cross-mandate retrieval incidents

personas.name: Mandate lead
personas.primaryJob: Keep a shared, current fact base for the mandate
personas.successMetric: Cited briefing ready before the next client meeting

personas.name: Analyst
personas.primaryJob: Interrogate the mandate corpus and draft defensible materials
personas.successMetric: Hours from document dump to cited memo

personas.name: Operator
personas.primaryJob: Control access, retention, and audit of research runs
personas.successMetric: Export a complete audit pack for any run in under five minutes

assumptions.assumption: Advisors will not trust uncited chatbot output for client work
INVRT's first painful job is cited briefing and diligence, not LBO/DCF model factories
Uploads plus public filings are enough to complete a useful MVP briefing
Mandate membership is the correct isolation boundary (not a single firm-wide corpus)
A boutique advisory will not buy an enterprise IB agent platform as its system of record

mvpScope.coreJob: Produce a cited target briefing (evidence table plus Word memo) from a mandate document corpus
inScope: Document ingest and citation index for PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX
Cited question answering with span-level or page-level sources
Evidence table (topics by questions) with per-cell citations
House-template Word memo with citation appendix and approve-to-export
Diligence question-list workflow from the same corpus
Immutable audit of retrieval, model version, actor, and cost
antiGoals: Bloomberg, Capital IQ, or PitchBook replacement
Scraping paid research or vendor logins
Hundreds of investment-banking agents in v1
PowerPoint pitchbooks and full DCF/LBO engines in MVP
Commercial multi-tenant SaaS launch in this inception

downstreamHandoff.entity-architect: Tenant, User, Role, WallGroup, Mandate, Membership, Party, Document, DocumentVersion, Chunk, Claim, Evidence, Locator, Playbook, Run, Artifact, Review, AgentDefinition, AgentRun, ToolCall, PromptVersion, EvidenceTable, TableCell, Memo, Export, AuditEvent, Connector, VendorEntitlement, IngestJob. Actors: analyst, lead, partner, reviewer, compliance, admin, worker. Verbs: create, invite, upload, ingest, index, query, fill, draft, revise, approve, export, retain, delete, offboard, wall_cross. Entity classes: Org, Identity, Domain, PlatformData, ExternalApi, AiAgent.
downstreamHandoff.ux-flow-designer: Journeys: first ingest, cited Q&A, evidence table edit, memo review and export, admin audit export. Entry: /mandates/:id. Error recovery: ingest failure, empty retrieval, citation reject, export blocked without approval.
downstreamHandoff.application-architect: Single JS API plus Python worker pool. Bounded contexts: identity, corpus, research run, work product, connectors, governance. Do not split microservices for MVP.
downstreamHandoff.billing-subscription-engineer: Skipped — internal tool, not monetised in this release.
downstreamHandoff.ai-feature-engineer: RAG plus tool calling plus table copilot. Risk tier high on export. Guardrails: tenant ACL on retrieval, input injection defense, output cite-or-refuse, tool allowlist, PII redaction in logs. Eval: citation coverage, citation precision, missing-fact honesty, numeric match, cross-mandate leak = 0.
downstreamHandoff.security-architect: Threat model: document prompt injection, cross-mandate RAG leak, export exfiltration, vendor subprocessors, no-train contractual controls, mandate offboarding.
